summary: Polars implementation of the expression system. PolarsExpressionSystem is assembled by multiple inheritance from per-family Substrait mixins (cast, conditional, field reference, literal, scalar and aggregate arithmetic/boolean/comparison/datetime/string/set/logarithmic/rounding, window, geometry) and Mountainash extension mixins (name, null, ternary, list, struct, categorical, geospatial, value, and others). It compiles the unified AST into native pl.Expr and is the only backend always imported. PolarsBaseExpressionSystem also supplies schema-based operand type resolution via LazyFrame.collect_schema.
key_classes: PolarsExpressionSystem — composed concrete backend registered for CONST_BACKEND.POLARS
PolarsBaseExpressionSystem — BACKEND_NAME='polars', is_native_expression (pl.Expr), operand-type resolution hooks
SubstraitPolars*ExpressionSystem — one mixin per Substrait protocol family under substrait/
MountainAshPolars*ExpressionSystem — mixins for Mountainash extension protocols under extensions_mountainash/
key_functions: cast_temporal_compatible(x, dtype, *, strict) — temporal-aware cast helper (temporal_cast.py)
cast_container(x, target, *, strict) — list/struct container cast (container_cast.py)
PolarsBaseExpressionSystem.field_operand_type(input_data, field) — maps schema dtype to OperandType without projection
extension_points: @register_expression_system(CONST_BACKEND.POLARS) registers the composed class with the visitor factory
declare_builtin_expression_system(<cls>, 'polars') declares the system for function-mapping lowering

Add an operation by implementing the protocol method in the matching substrait/ or extensions_mountainash/ expsys_*_<family> mixin, which is composed by multiple inheritance (backend-composition principle)
Override BaseExpressionSystem hooks (is_native_expression, field_operand_type, infer_expression_operand_type, fixed_result_type)

risks: Large mixin sets: method-name collisions across inheritance are a hazard (guarded by test_mro_method_collisions)
expsys_pl_scalar_string.py (~1300 lines) and arithmetic/datetime files are complexity hotspots
Polars is the reference backend; behaviour differences in Narwhals/Ibis are documented as capability facts rather than fixed here
__init__ __all__ omits several extension mixins that are imported and composed (e.g. List, Struct, Categorical, Aggregate), so __all__ is not an exhaustive list of composed parts

evidence.detail: PolarsExpressionSystem composed by multiple inheritance and decorated with @register_expression_system(CONST_BACKEND.POLARS), followed by declare_builtin_expression_system
Polars is always imported; Narwhals and Ibis imported only if installed
backend-composition principle (each backend composes all protocol implementations via multiple inheritance)
Cross-backend parametrized tests exercise this system (cross-backend-test-coverage principle)
